title: Your client tracker, follow-up rhythm and client feedback

say: Your client tracker, your follow-up rhythm, and client feedback.
This is the video for module 2 of Client Relationship Management.
Make a spreadsheet called Client tracker with two tabs. Clients has one row per person, with her details and next action. Orders has one row per order, so Sheets can add up her history for you.

say: Add drop-down lists, so a status is always written the same way: New, Active, Quiet or Lapsed. Link the client names in Orders to the client list, so every name is spelled exactly the same.

say: Test your formulas once with a calculator, so you can trust them.

card.title: Check the formulas once by hand

say: Ngozi's Orders tab shows 4 orders for Ifeoma: 18,000, 22,000, 18,000 and 25,000 naira.

card.title: Check the formulas once by hand

say: That adds up to 83,000 naira, the same as the sheet.
But one order had been typed as Ifeoma with an extra space, and the count missed it. That is exactly why drop-down lists matter. Also type amounts as plain numbers, without the naira sign.

say: Many problems start before delivery, when the client and the business understood different things. One thought Friday meant morning. The other meant evening.

panel.heading: A clear order confirmation
items: Total price, and what it includes
Deposit, and when the balance is due
Changes allowed, and how you will update her

say: So once she agrees, send a short WhatsApp confirmation covering these five points, and ask her to reply confirmed.
Save it as a quick reply, and change the details each time.

say: Send a confirmation on day 0, a progress update before delivery, and a handover note on delivery day.

panel.heading: Five touches for every order

say: On day 3, send a short after-care check. I hope the trays went well at the meeting. Was the quantity right for your guests?

panel.heading: Five touches for every order

say: And remind her when she is likely to need you again.
Do not crowd her. Between orders, send no more than one non-sales message a month, unless she starts the conversation.

panel.heading: Five touches for every order

say: For example, Funmi supplies liquid soap to Halima's provisions shop. Halima ordered on 3 February, 1 March, 4 April and 2 May.

panel.heading: Funmi works out Halima's reorder gap
items: Remind a few days early: 28 May

say: From her first order to her last is 88 days.

panel.heading: Funmi works out Halima's reorder gap
items: Remind a few days early: 28 May

say: 4 orders means 3 gaps. 88 divided by 3 is about 29 days. That is her reorder gap.

panel.heading: Funmi works out Halima's reorder gap
items: Remind a few days early: 28 May

say: So Funmi messages on 28 May: your last delivery was 2 May. Shall I bring the usual 6 kegs on Friday?
Halima is reminded before she runs out, so she does not buy elsewhere.

panel.heading: Funmi works out Halima's reorder gap
items: Remind a few days early: 28 May

say: Clients rarely announce that they are leaving. A healthy relationship looks like steady orders, replies and referrals.

panel.heading: Healthy signs and warning signs

say: Warning signs are longer gaps, smaller orders and unanswered messages. One sign may mean nothing. Two or more are worth a gentle, honest check-in. Do not guilt her. Ask whether your service still fits her needs.

panel.heading: Healthy signs and warning signs

say: Ask 2 or 3 short questions, including: on a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend me to a friend?
For example, Ruth tutors pupils in Lagos and asks 20 parents. 12 answer 9 or 10. They are promoters, 60 percent.

panel.heading: Net Promoter Score, step by step

cards.d: Ruth asks 20 parents. 12 answer 9 or 10. That is 60 percent.
5 parents. They are not used in the formula.
3 parents, which is 15 percent. NPS is 60 minus 15, which is 45.

say: 5 answer 7 or 8. They are passives, and are left out.

3 parents, which is 15 percent. NPS is 60 minus 15, which is 45.

say: 3 answer 6 or lower. They are detractors, 15 percent. Her score is 60 minus 15, which is 45.
More useful still, two detractors said lesson times changed without notice. So Ruth now gives a week's notice of any change.

say: To remember. Keep one row per client and one per order. Confirm every order in writing. Before you mark an order as Paid, check your bank app, because a screenshot is not proof of payment.
Time reminders from her own reorder gap. And when a client gives feedback, change one thing and tell her you did.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One row per client, one row per order
Check payments in your bank app, not screenshots
Remind clients from their own reorder gap
Act on one piece of feedback, then tell her

say: Now practise. Build your tracker with at least 10 real clients and test one total by hand. Save your confirmation as a quick reply and work out three reorder gaps. Then send the feedback questions to five clients and calculate your score.
